messages.subject: Using older packages on newer R versions
parts:
Hi all,

After installing R 3.0 (how exciting!) I found that many packages that I like are not available for this new version of R. Is there an easy way to bypass this, should I stick to an older version of R, or should I pester the package authors? 

Thanks very much, and if you just want to respond to me my email is mawh...@ucdavis.edu.

messages.author: 8c8f0ca54c4a2459
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Using older packages on newer R versions
parts:
Hey Matt,

A few thoughts, which may or may not help you:

 - You probably thought of this, but I didn't at first: when you run `update.packages`, make sure you include `checkBuilt=TRUE`, otherwise packages don't update to the new version of R.
 - I'm not sure if this would work, but I wonder if you can download the package source and build it yourself.  If there is some process that package authors need to initiate to make sure the binaries are updated, then maybe the sources are just fine if you build them locally.  Does anybody know more about this?
 - When you install a new version of R, by default it leaves the last version on your machine unless you delete it manually.  You can switch between the versions as needed.  Instructions here: http://www.rstudio.com/ide/docs/advanced/versions_of_r
 - An older version of R is probably good enough until the packages you want stop being compatible

Noam
